stemMarkdown: A 45-litre solution contains 36% acid. How many litres of water must be added to dilute it to a 30% acid solution? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The acid stays fixed at $16.20$ litres. For that to be $30\%$ of the solution, the total volume must become $\dfrac{16.20 \times 100}{30} = 54.00$ litres. Water to add $= 54.00 - 45 = 9.0$ litres.
altSolutionMarkdown: Only the solvent changes — anchoring on the unchanged solute is what makes these quick.
